# Scanpy source inventory

Repository: [scverse/scanpy](https://github.com/scverse/scanpy)  
Inspected revision: `8c1463d5d97272d5811ad3f4efb57483e23b4c7e` (resolved by runner through the GitHub commits API; repository contents read at this immutable revision).  
Retrieval date: 2026-09-30 UTC.  
Coverage: 11 units and 8 dataset/reference records. This is a documented-example pass, not an execution or task-validation pass.

Scanpy is a Python toolkit for single-cell gene-expression analysis using AnnData. README describes preprocessing, visualization, clustering, trajectory inference and differential-expression testing. Inspected examples support QC and doublet detection, basic multi-sample preprocessing/clustering and marker interpretation, reference-to-query label/embedding transfer, batch graph integration, trajectory graph abstraction/pseudotime and cell-cycle scoring/regression. The inventory prioritizes these distinct scientific uses. Source inspection does not establish successful execution, Harbor compatibility, suitable deterministic graders or data redistribution rights.

## Recorded scientific units

`units.jsonl` contains 11 unique records. Three records separate the newer clustering tutorial's QC/doublet, core preprocessing/clustering, and marker/DE activities; they share one identified bone-marrow dataset and form an upstream chain. The legacy Seurat-style PBMC3k workflow is a distinct data context and documented comparison workflow (`scanpy-pbmc3k-legacy-seurat-clustering`), not a duplicate of those units. Pearson-residual feature selection and transformation on two PBMC datasets are separate from that legacy workflow because they use a distinct preprocessing model and comparison. The trajectory record combines the linked Paul15 preprocessing, graph construction, abstraction, embedding and pseudotime stages because the tutorial frames them as one hematopoietic trajectory reconstruction. The cell-cycle how-to is a separate expression-covariate correction use. The ingest tutorial is split between PBMC reference transfer and joint BBKNN comparison, and pancreas graph integration and batch-to-reference mapping/evaluation, because these are distinct data contexts and questions. IDs use source/tutorial identity plus operation rather than discovery order.

All eight units are classified `tool_use`: each example composes Scanpy or an external package on existing biological data. Reading the Scanpy implementation clarified operation contracts but the inspected tutorial sources do not implement those tools. Unit inputs/outputs describe documented AnnData slots and tutorial outputs; plots are not interpreted as validated grades.

## Data reconciliation and provenance

`datasets.jsonl` contains 7 records. It keeps separate the Open Problems bone-marrow multiome tutorial input, Paul15 study observations, Nestorowa expression input, Tirosh gene-list reference, PBMC3k raw/processed product, PBMC68k query, and curated multi-study pancreas collection. PBMC3k raw and processed states are assets in one record because the loader explicitly documents the processed object as the basic-tutorial derivative of the same healthy-donor source. The 68k object is separate. The pancreas Dropbox H5AD and Sanger BBKNN ZIP are left as separate assets of unresolved relationship; no download or metadata check demonstrated they are identical products. Tirosh gene symbols are a reference product separate from Nestorowa observations despite appearing in the same ZIP.

Retrieved file sizes and hashes are only those supplied in GitHub tree/registry metadata: the PBMC68k bundled archive size and the registry SHA-256 values for Paul15 and processed PBMC3k. Other asset byte sizes, content hashes, current availability and redistribution rights are unknown. The tutorial's DOI/links are evidence of intended access, not terms permission. No biological files were downloaded or previewed. No study record was inferred beyond tutorial citation/source text; unknown accession and detailed design fields remain unresolved.

## Access notes, gaps, and stopping point

The GitHub recursive tree request reported `truncated=false`; a broad result exceeded display limits, so a filtered path/size listing was used to locate relevant documentation and source. All inspected GitHub files were read at revision `8c1463d5d97272d5811ad3f4efb57483e23b4c7e`. Two guessed paths `src/scanpy/pp/_qc.py` and `src/scanpy/pp/_normalization.py` returned GitHub HTTP 404; the package sources are under `src/scanpy/preprocessing/`, and the task proceeds using official notebook/API docs plus the corrected package path for highly-variable genes. The source map remains partial: Dask/tutorial plotting/API pages and multiple API entries remain available leads. The hard stop time was `2026-09-30T14:37:52.007121Z`; a clock check at `2026-09-30 14:45:17 UTC` confirms the limit had elapsed by final review. Further source discovery stopped at that actual time limit. No access or resource limit prevented the remaining leads; continue with `docs/tutorials/experimental/dask.ipynb`, the plotting/how-to notebooks, and pending API entries in a fresh pass.

## Facts and task hypotheses

Source-backed facts are the documented biological settings, API sequence, observed inputs and outputs, and explicit caveats captured in unit/dataset records. Possible task hypotheses include grading QC metrics or filter decisions on fixed data, transfer of reference labels, checking preservation of cell types alongside batch mixing, or matching trajectory annotations/pseudotime. These remain hypotheses: no task prompt, supplied starting artifact, expected output, executable grader, resource estimate or license review has been validated.
